This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri. Mahesh Sathi Gowda in a Road Traffic Accident.
2. The petition averments in brief is that:-
The petitioners are claiming they are the wife, son and father of deceased Mahesha.

On 02.01.2018 at about 10.00 a.m., the deceased Sri. Mahesh was a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EB-6873 when they reached Holenarasipura Road towards Goruru-Hebbale near Ganjalgudu, at that time the rider of the motor cycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and jumped into the left side of the road which leads to channel along with motor cycle.
Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Thereafter the dead body was shifted to Hassan Jyothi vs Manje Gowda on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100107504/

Thereafter he was referred to NIMHANS Hospital for higher treatment, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for about 10 days and was discharged and then shifted to Janashri Hospital, Hassan for further treatment, wherein he didn't respond to the treatment and was dead on 22.01.2018.
The petitioners have spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food  SCCH-9 4 MVC.No.2186/2018 and nourishment, conveyance, transportation, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was a farmer and earning Rs.6,00,000/- p.a.
The petitioners have lost all his income, the deceased was the only bread earner of their family and all the family members were depending upon deceased for their livelihood.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle.
In this regard, a case has been registered in the jurisdictional Police Station.

The respondents being owner and Insurer of the motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners, who are wife, child and father of deceased and lost their bread earner in the accident.

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1: In the negative.
Issue No.2: In the negative.
Issue No.1:-

It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 02.01.2018 at bout 10.00 a.m., the deceased Mahesh S/o Sathi Gowda was met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider in which deceased Mahesh was a pillion rider and  SCCH-9 8 MVC.No.2186/2018 due to said accident deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to death.

9. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 has filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and examined as PW1 and reiterated all the facts mentioned in her petition and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P14.

The Ex.P1 is the FIR & complaint, Ex.P2 is the inquest mahazar, Ex.P3 is the rough sketch, Ex.P.4 is the mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, Ex.P6 is PM report, Ex.P7 Charge Sheet, Ex.P8 is the ration card, Ex.P.9 to 12 are the Aadhaar cards of petitioners, Ex.P.13 is medical bills and Ex.P14 is the prescriptions.
10 . On perusal of these documents, it shows wife of deceased by name Jyothi W/o.

Mahesh.S, who is also a petitioner No.1 herein had lodged First Information before Arkalugudu Police Station, alleging that on 02.01.2018, her hsuband deceased Mahesh was proceeding motorcycle Jyothi vs Manje Gowda on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100107504/
6 bearing No.KA-13-EB-6378 as a pillion rider and he met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of rider of said  SCCH-9 9 MVC.No.2186/2018 motor cycle.

On the basis of this first Information the Arakalagudu Police have registered the case in Cr.No.15/2018 for the offence punishable Under Sec.279,
337 of IPC R/w sec.187 of MV Act.

Thereafter, the Investigation Officer had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the deceased by name Mahesha.S for the offence punishable Under Sec. 279 &
304(A) of IPC.
 11.
The respondent No.2 has mainly contended that deceased was not a pillion rider.
The deceased himself was a rider and drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
Since deceased was a tortfeasor the petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act for compensation cannot be maintainable.
12. The official of respondent No.2 examined as RW2 and go marked Ex.R4 to R6.
In the chief examination this RW2 mainly contended that deceased was a not a pillion rider.
The deceased was a rider and he himself caused the accident.
Since deceased was a tortfeasor the  SCCH-9 10 MVC.No.2186/2018 petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act by legal heirs of deceased is not maintainable.

The learned counsel for petitioners Jyothi vs Manje Gowda on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100107504/
7 submitted that he has no cross to RW2.
Therefore it shows that the evidence of RW2 remained unchallenged and uncontested.
13. I have perused entire materials available on record.
As stated above, the petitioners alleging that deceased was a pillion rider and one Puneeth Kumar was a rider at the time of accident.
It is material to note that the Arakalugudu Police have filed the charge sheet to the Court.
In the charge sheet vide Ex.P7 it is stated that the deceased Mahesh. S was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-13-EB- 6873 with rash and negligent manner and himself caused the accident.
Further in Ex.R2 MLC record it has mentioned that "alleged history RTA skid and fall from two wheeler".

The PW1, who is wife of deceased in her evidence stated that her husband was a pillion rider and rider has caused the accident, but for proving this aspect the petitioners have not produced any documents.
However the petitioners tried to prove the fact that the deceased was  SCCH-9 11 MVC.No.2186/2018 a pillion rider and one Puneeth Kumar was a rider by examining witness PW2/Puneeth Kumar.

The PW2/Puneeth Kumar.U.M., who is alleged rider in his evidence deposed that he was riding the alleged motor cycle and deceased Mahesh was a pillion rider at the time of accident and due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle the accident was caused.

But in the cross-examination this PW2/Puneet Kumar has clearly stated that he has no bother to file the Jyothi vs Manje Gowda on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100107504/
8 complaint after the accident.
The wife of deceased has lodged the complaint.
He did not brought the deceased Mahesh to the NIMHANS.

It is crucial to note that the learned counsel for respondent No.2 suggested that Police have filed the charge sheet stating that - "while Mahesh riding the motorcycle it was skid and jumped into channel and sustained injury".
The PW2 has not denied said suggestion but pleads ignorance.
If this PW2 was rider of motorcycle why he did not brought the deceased into hospital.
Moreover, the investigating officer has not cited this PW2 as a witness.
It is also material to note that according to petitioners at the time of accident both rider  SCCH-9 12 MVC.No.2186/2018 and pillion rider fell down left side channel.
If that is so there could be some injuries to rider also.
But there is no injuries caused to PW.2.
These aspect also create doubt on the evidence of PW2.
Except oral testimony of PW1 and PW2 there is nothing on record to show deceased was pillion rider at the time of accident.
Therefore, the evidence of PW2 is not helpful to the case of the petitioners to establish deceased was a pillion rider and PW2 was a rider.
14. If rider of vehicle himself caused the accident by rash and negligent riding and became tortfeasor, the petition U/sec 166 Motor Vehicle by the legal heirs is not maintainable.

This preposition of law was held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment reported in (2018) 9 Jyothi vs Manje Gowda on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100107504/
9 SCC 801 (NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. V/S ASHALATA BHOWMIK AND ORS.) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court was please to held at para 7 as under:-

sentences.text: "We have carefully considered the submissions of the  learned counsel made at the Bar and perused the  materials placed on record.
It is an admitted position  that the deceased was the owner-cum-driver of the  vehicle in question.
The accident had occurred due to  the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by the  deceased.
No other vehicle was involved in the accident.
The deceased himself was responsible for the accident.
SCCH-9 13 MVC.No.2186/2018  The deceased being the owner of the offending vehicle  was not a third party within the meaning of the Act.
The  deceased was the victim of his own action of rash and  negligent driving.

A Claimant, in our view, cannot  maintain a claim on the basis of his own fault or  negligence and argue that even when he himself  may have caused the accident on account of his  own rash and negligent driving, he can  nevertheless make the insurance company to pay  for the same.
Therefore, the respondents being  the LRs of the deceased could not have  maintained the claim petition filed under Section  166 of the Motor Vehicles Act."

15. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a judgment in a case between The Divisional Manager V/s Rayan Fernandes & anr. (MFA 7279/2016 C/W 7110/2016 (MV)) Wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka was please to held at para No.16 as under:-
 "Since the clinching rebuttal evidence clearly  demonstrates that the claimant himself was riding the  bike and on account of his own negligence he sustained  injuries, the claimant cannot maintain petition either  against the Insurance Company or the first respondent-  owner."

sentences.text: The conduct  of the Investigating Officer clearly shows that he is  extending his helping hand to the petitioners.
So also  the Medical Officers, who tampered the very MLC  Register to help the petitioners to get the compensation.
The Court is also having greater sympathy towards the  petitioners that they have lost their bread-earner.
But  they being losing their son while doing wheeling in the  bicycle cannot be a bonanza or wind-fall to make a false
claim against a motor bike which is in no way connected
to the accident

On appreciation of entire evidence available on record it is held that deceased was a rider and he himself caused the accident by rash and negligent riding of vehicle,
then the petition u/Sec 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is not maintainable.
The judgment referred above are aptly applicable to the present case on hand as the facts and circumstances of the above referred judgment are same to the present case on hand.
As such it is also held that the  SCCH-9 15 MVC.No.2186/2018 petitioners have failed to prove the issue No.1.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.1 in the Negative.

11  18. Issue No.2:
Since petitioners failed to prove the Issue No.1 they are not entitled for any compensation from the Court.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Negative.
19. Issue No.3:

For the aforesaid reasons and discussion, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
